craft_claim: Positive-politeness moves (in-group markers, seeking agreement, joking, including the reader in the activity, attending to the reader's wants) are the linguistic signature of the warm voice.

supporting_evidence.location: Politeness: Some Universals in Language Usage, ch. 5, positive-politeness output strategies
supporting_evidence.note: Catalogues approach-based redress strategies oriented to the addressee's positive face, including noticing wants, intensifying interest, in-group identity markers, seeking agreement, presupposing common ground, joking, including both parties, and assuming reciprocity.
The narrators treat ordinary characters' failings with affectionate irony, inviting the reader into shared amusement rather than judgement, an instance of searching for agreement and shared ground.
Sa'di frames severe moral counsel as a friend's advice, mixing instruction with wit so the reader is included in the exchange rather than lectured.

counterevidence.note: Leech's sociopragmatic scale registers overpoliteness as a potential sarcasm, so the strategies fail when they exceed what the situation warrants.

scope: Conversational and direct-address writing across forms; the strategies require a plausible relationship to be genuine.
exceptions: High-formality registers where positive politeness would violate expected negative-face respect.
Cultures whose warmth forms differ from Anglophone positive politeness (see dossier E).
